name: Soluna Holdings, Inc.

profile.description: Soluna Holdings develops and operates modular data centers co-located with wind, solar, and hydro sites, converting otherwise-curtailed renewable power into computing capacity for Bitcoin mining hosting, proprietary mining, and AI/high-performance computing workloads. Projects include Dorothy (Texas), Sophie (Kentucky), and Kati (Texas). Formerly Mechanical Technology Inc. (founded 1961), it renamed in November 2021. John Belizaire is CEO.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): Soluna sold off MTI's legacy instruments business and rebuilt itself around renewable-sited data centers, and Q2 2026 revenue of $15.1M (+145% YoY) marked a fifth straight quarter of sequential growth, with TTM revenue of $42.1M versus $27.9M a year earlier [1][2]. AI Deployment (1/2): The Kati 2 AI data center joint venture with Metrobloks and the Helix AI-training upgrade show AI hosting is being built, but AI revenue is not reported separately from Bitcoin hosting [1][4]. Market Share (0/2): With 51 employees and roughly 0.1 GW operating, Soluna is a niche participant beside hyperscale and large mining-hosting peers. Pipeline (1/2): The development pipeline expanded to about 6.3 GW and Kati 1 reached its first gross profit, but named projects lack firm energization dates and contracted AI tenants [1]. R&D Intensity (0/1): No disclosed R&D program; spending is project capex, not R&D [3].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (3/4): Soluna's stated purpose to 'make renewable energy a global superpower, using computing as a catalyst' is specific and ties its data centers to solving curtailed, stranded clean power, which differentiates it from generic miners [3]. Community Impact (0/2): No quantified charitable or community investment programs were found [5]. Employee Retention (0/2): The finance seat turned over again with Michael Picchi named CFO in January 2026 after an interim period, and no retention data is published [6]. Insider Buying (0/2): CEO John Belizaire owns about 4.1% largely through stock awards (total pay about $2.18M); no meaningful open-market insider purchases were identified, while the company relies on ATM issuance [1][7].

infrastructure.label: DEVELOPING
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored as a Growth stock on six available metrics (total weight 8). D/E of 18.6% scores 1.0 (x1); ROE of -68.4% scores 0.0 (x2); revenue growth of 144.6% YoY scores 1.0 (x1); 5yr revenue CAGR of about 30% (from roughly $10M in MTI's 2020 base to $42.1M TTM) scores 1.0 (x2); Forward P/E of -2.85 (negative) scores 0.0 (x1); and profit margin of -182% scores 0.0 (x1) [1][8]. Forward PEG is excluded because forward earnings are negative. Weighted sum 4.0/8 = 5.0, giving a score of 5; Q2 net loss widened to about $20.7-22.6M and gross profit fell to $0.8M. Liquidity floor cleared: 9.48M avg shares x $0.65 = $6.2M daily dollar volume [8].

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (8/9): Soluna sells physical power-and-compute capacity, so AI is a demand driver rather than a substitute; the Kati 2 AI data center JV and Helix AI-training retrofit position its renewable sites for AI workloads [1][4]. Risk stems from execution and Bitcoin economics, not from AI displacement. AI Opportunity (0/1): AI/HPC revenue is not quantified separately from Bitcoin hosting in Q2 2026 disclosures, so the tiebreaker is not awarded [1][2].

infinite_game.summary: Sinek would credit Soluna for a genuinely distinctive idea, putting stranded renewable power to work, but the company's behavior is that of a capital-hungry survivor: repeated ATM dilution, deep losses ($53.4M in 2025, $63.3M in 2024), and a strategy that has tracked the Bitcoin and then AI cycles [1][8]. The cause is real; whether it shapes hard trade-offs is unproven.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): Making renewable energy a 'global superpower' through computing is idealistic, service-oriented, and distinct from peers, and CEO Belizaire references it consistently [3]. It has not yet been tested across decades or leadership transitions.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Leadership kept building Dorothy and Kati through the crypto winter and absorbed a $28.6M loss to exit the Hewlett Packard Enterprise AI cloud contract rather than carry a misaligned commitment [5]. That courage is funded by heavy dilution rather than internally generated cash.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (0/2): A 51-person organization with repeated CFO changes (interim CFO David Michaels, then Michael Picchi in January 2026) and no public evidence of retention or empowerment practices [6]. Compensation is skewed toward stock awards amid ongoing losses [7].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Soluna transformed from MTI, a 60-year-old instruments maker, into a data center developer and is now repositioning from Bitcoin hosting to AI, a dramatic shift [3][4]. Each pivot followed market momentum (crypto, then AI) more than the Just Cause, so it falls short of full credit.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): No management commentary was found that frames larger hosting and AI data center peers as benchmarks to learn from; messaging focuses on Soluna's own pipeline and differentiation [1].

investment_thesis: Soluna is growing quickly from a small base: Q2 2026 revenue rose 145% to $15.1M, TTM revenue reached $42.1M, and consensus expects about $61.8M of 2026 revenue [1][2]. The company vertically integrated the 50 MW Dorothy 1 site, Kati 1 reached first gross profit, a Metrobloks JV targets the Kati 2 AI data center, and the development pipeline expanded to roughly 6.3 GW [1]. With over $113M of cash against $39M of debt (D/E 18.6%), Soluna has runway to convert renewable-sited land and power into AI hosting capacity, a model that AI power demand directly favors [8].
thesis_continued: The bear case is profitability and dilution. Net losses were $53.4M in 2025 and $63.3M in 2024, Q2 2026 net loss widened to about $20.7-22.6M, gross profit fell to $0.8M on ramp and maintenance costs, and free cash flow is about -$40M [1][8]. Q2 revenue missed the $15.7M consensus. Growth is funded through ATM equity sales, and the share price has fallen to $0.65 from a 50-day average of $1.03, raising Nasdaq minimum-bid risk. Sustainalytics rates ESG risk 'High' at 31.4, and Bitcoin price swings still drive much of revenue [5].
key_catalysts: Signing a creditworthy AI/HPC tenant for Kati 2 under the Metrobloks joint venture, converting pipeline into contracted AI revenue [1]
Q3 2026 results (consensus about $18.1M revenue) showing gross margin recovery after Dorothy 1 integration and Kati 1 profitability [1][2]
Monetizing part of the ~6.3 GW renewable-sited pipeline through JV partnerships that reduce Soluna's equity funding needs [1]
key_risks: Ongoing dilution from ATM equity sales to fund losses (free cash flow about -$40M) with the stock below $1 and at risk of a Nasdaq bid-price notice [8]
Bitcoin price and network-hashrate swings that compress hosting and mining economics, which still make up most revenue [1]
Execution risk in converting renewable-sited Bitcoin infrastructure to AI-grade data centers, highlighted by the $28.6M loss on the terminated HPE contract [5]
